Introduce the F‑statistic as a ratio of variances: variation between groups divided by variation within groups.

explanation: [[kw:One‑way analysis of variance (ANOVA)]] compares the means of three or more populations to see if at least one is different.
The null hypothesis: $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \dots = \mu_k$ (all means are equal).
The alternative: $H_a$: At least one mean is different.
ANOVA works by comparing two types of variation: [[imp:variance between samples]] (how much the sample means differ) and [[imp:variance within samples]] (how much the data vary inside each group).
If the between‑group variation is large relative to the within‑group variation, it suggests the population means are not all equal.

formulaCard.formula: $$ H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \dots = \mu_k $$ $$ H_a: \text{At least one mean is different} $$
notes: ANOVA is always right‑tailed: reject for large F.
We don't know which mean is different without further testing.

confusionCorner.title: MSB vs. MSW: Don't Mix Them Up
confusionCorner.body: MSB is based on differences among sample means. MSW is a pooled average of the individual sample variances. [[imp:MSB reflects treatment effects; MSW reflects random error.]]

teacherCues: Draw two sets of boxplots: one with tight boxes but far apart, another with overlapping boxes. Ask: In which case is F large?
Write F = MSB / MSW. Explain MSB (Mean Square Between) and MSW (Mean Square Within).

explanation: The test statistic for one‑way ANOVA is $$F = \frac{MSB}{MSW}$$
[[kw:MSB]] (Mean Square Between) estimates the variance between groups. It is large when the sample means are far apart.
[[kw:MSW]] (Mean Square Within) estimates the variance within groups. It pools the sample variances.
If $H_0$ is true, MSB and MSW are similar, so $F \approx 1$. If $H_0$ is false, MSB > MSW, so $F > 1$.
Degrees of freedom: numerator $d.f._N = k - 1$ (k = number of groups), denominator $d.f._D = N - k$ (N = total observations).

notes: Reject $H_0$ if $F$ > critical value from F‑table (Table 7).
Google Sheets: use `=F.DIST.RT(F, d.f.N, d.f.D)` for p‑value.

blocks.title: The ANOVA F‑Statistic: Between vs. Within Variation

teacherCues: Walk through the pain reliever data step by step: find sample means, grand mean, SSB, SSW, MSB, MSW, F.
Show the shortcut formulas for SSB and SSW.

notes: $\bar{x}$ = grand mean = total of all values / N.
Google Sheets can perform ANOVA via `=F.TEST` on two groups at a time, but for multiple groups, use add‑ons or manual calculations.
formulaCard.formula: $$ SSB = \sum n_i (\bar{x}_i - \bar{x})^2 $$ $$ SSW = \sum (n_i - 1) s_i^2 $$ $$ MSB = \frac{SSB}{k-1}, \quad MSW = \frac{SSW}{N-k} $$ $$ F = \frac{MSB}{MSW} $$
formulaCard.title: Key ANOVA Formulas

explanation: 1. Compute each sample mean $\bar{x}_i$ and the [[kw:grand mean]] $\bar{x}$ (mean of all observations).
2. [[kw:SSB]] (Sum of Squares Between): $$SSB = \sum n_i (\bar{x}_i - \bar{x})^2$$
3. [[kw:SSW]] (Sum of Squares Within): $$SSW = \sum (n_i - 1) s_i^2$$ (or compute directly from data).
4. $MSB = SSB / (k-1)$, $MSW = SSW / (N-k)$.
5. $F = MSB / MSW$.
For the pain reliever data: $\bar{x}_1=14$, $\bar{x}_2=17$, $\bar{x}_3=16.5$, grand mean $=15.92$, $SSB \approx 21.92$, $SSW = 73$, $MSB = 10.96$, $MSW = 7.3$, $F = 1.50$.

confusionCorner.title: SSW Uses Variances, Not Standard Deviations
confusionCorner.body: The formula $SSW = \sum (n_i-1)s_i^2$ uses variances. If you are given standard deviations, square them first.
